scope: the two-operand bootstrap, the destination-local justfile, the deployed lifecycle that needs nothing but the destination, the source-side wrappers that take at most a DESTINATION, and the repository preparation the two-argument operation performs. the_deployed_justfile.it_is_an_owned_path: custody refuses a link at that name and never replaces an existing one
the_deployed_justfile.not_a_login_shell: the first live run printed a profile permission error before every recipe; a deployed command must not depend on whoever's profile happens to be readable where it runs
the_deployed_justfile.nothing_beneath_it_was_loosened: every recipe still passes --instance, so the command still verifies the whole runtime and still refuses another instance's selector
the_deployed_justfile.resolves_from_itself: HERE := justfile_directory(), and COMMAND and INSTANCE derive from HERE, which is what makes --justfile mean the same deployment as cd
the_deployed_justfile.written_by: bootstrap.install, from bootstrap.deployed_justfile, before the selector -- so a destination carrying a selector always carries the justfile that drives it

the_repositories.and_it_names_them: repositories_bound puts those paths into the emitted configuration where the input did not already choose
the_repositories.this_agent_ran_none_of_it: the repository tool is invoked through an injectable runner and every check here substitutes it. This Work performs no version-control mutation; the owner invokes the finished operation.
the_repositories.what_it_does: with `repository_source` named, it prepares <destination>/repo/target.git (a mirror of the owner's source), <destination>/repo/workspace and one <destination>/repo/source-<worker_id> per worker -- each a separate --no-local clone, so each has its own object store -- and then PROVES them: every one identifies itself, no two are one repository or one directory, none borrows objects, and the target holds every declared base and the configured import reference
the_repositories.what_the_owner_directed: the two-argument bootstrap creates the bundled distro, databases AND independent repositories
the_repositories.when_no_source_is_named: nothing is cloned and the install says so: missing production choices do not prevent building and testing the generic owner-run command

what_the_interface_change_COST_and_where.the_limit: a self-contained deployment cannot prove its own launcher's bytes before that launcher runs; nothing inside it is outside it. A changed library, frozen asset, unbound extra file or foreign selector is still refused.
what_the_interface_change_COST_and_where.what: the source recipe used to ask `tools.instance command`, which verified the runtime and only then printed a path to exec, so a changed LAUNCHER never ran. The deployed interface has no checkout to ask: it runs the command, and the command verifies its own instance before deriving anything.
what_the_interface_change_COST_and_where.where_it_is_said: v12/STACK.md, and a focused check (test_the_runtime_CHECK_moved_into_the_command_and_this_says_so) that drives stack.main with instance.verify refusing and requires exit 2. The four stand-in 'never executes' cases were REMOVED rather than left passing for the wrong reason: a printing stand-in cannot verify itself.
